reading.objective: Fill a small room for one night with three independent bands
reading.audience: Local gig-goers in Leith and Edinburgh who read posters on walls
reading.feeling: Quiet, salt-air, slightly melancholy, then warm like boiler light

concept.idea: The sheet is a tidal flat: a dark body of water has pulled back to a wavering shoreline, leaving the title stranded at the water's edge and the details on the exposed sand.
decisions: structure: weight sits in the lower half of the dark mass, with an empty dark sky above it; the shoreline is the hinge between title and details
read first: the huge 'Low Tide' standing on the waterline
type: Instrument Serif at a very large size for the title, tightly set; Instrument Sans for the small print so details stay crisp
colour: dark marsh green-black water, pale salt-bone sand, and one boiler-orange line along the shore and on the call to action
forms: one drawn shoreline, one band of wet sand with faint ripples; nothing else
